solution: Rewrite using \(1-\log_{10}5=\log_{10}2\): the equation becomes \(\log_{10}\big(2^x(1+2^x)/6\big)=0\), so \(2^x(1+2^x)=6\). Let \(y=2^x\): \(y^2+y-6=0\Rightarrow(y-2)(y+3)=0\Rightarrow y=2\) (rejecting \(y=-3\)). Then \(2^x=2\Rightarrow x=1\). Matches option C: 1. Note that \(y=2\) is the value of \(2^x\), not of \(x\).

Expanding both determinants gives \(\Delta_1=\Delta_2=-(p^2+q^2+r^2-pq-qr-rp)=-\tfrac12\big[(p-q)^2+(q-r)^2+(r-p)^2\big]\). Hence \(\Delta_1+\Delta_2=2\Delta_1=-\big[(p-q)^2+(q-r)^2+(r-p)^2\big]\), which is negative for distinct \(p,q,r\). Matches option C: always negative.

AP gives \(2b=a+c\); GP gives \(c^2=bd\); HP gives \(\tfrac{2}{d}=\tfrac1c+\tfrac1e\). Eliminating \(b\) and \(d\) yields \(c^2=ae\), so \(a,c,e\) are in GP, hence (A) holds. The reciprocals of any GP form a GP, so \(\tfrac1a,\tfrac1c,\tfrac1e\) are in GP; equivalently \((1/c)^2=1/(ae)=1/c^2\). Thus (B) holds as well. Matches option C: Both A and B.

Statement 1: \((A\cap B)\cup(A\cap\bar B)\cup(\bar A\cap B)=A\cup(\bar A\cap B)=A\cup B\), which is true. Statement 2: \(A\cup(\bar A\cap\bar B)=(A\cup\bar A)\cap(A\cup\bar B)=A\cup\bar B\), which is not equal to \(A\cup B\) in general, so it is false. Only statement 1 is correct. Matches option A: 1 only.
